public_rationale: Zitron says an internal Microsoft document told managers to use Copilot to summarize their reports' Connects, Perspectives and feedback as a basis for drafting reward and promotion justifications. I searched for Microsoft guidance, Microsoft statements and news reports that confirm or deny this. Later reporting covers different things: a 2025 memo telling managers to weigh employees' AI use, and public tips for using Copilot on self-reviews. None of it speaks to this guidance on reward justifications. Nothing contradicts the claim either. The claim rests only on a document the speaker says he saw, so it stays unresolved.
limitations: The guidance is internal and not public. Missing confirmation is not evidence the claim is false.
I could not search Microsoft's internal systems or paywalled Business Insider archives in full.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft instructs managers to use Copilot to summarize direct reports' Connects and feedback as a basis for drafting reward and promotion justifications.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft is also — as I learned from an internal document I’ve reviewed — instructing managers to use it to summarize "their direct report's Connects, Perspectives and other feedback collected throughout the fiscal year as a basis to draft Rewards/promotion justifications in the Manage Rewards Tool (MRI),"

from_speaker: as I learned from an internal document I've reviewed
to summarize their direct report's Connects, Perspectives and other feedback
as a basis to draft Rewards/promotion justifications in the Manage Rewards Tool
our_interpretation: The claim is about what Microsoft's internal guidance said: managers were told (or encouraged in official guidance) to use Copilot to summarize a report's Connects, Perspectives and other feedback, and to use that summary as a starting point for drafting reward or promotion justifications.
This tests the speaker's narrow factual claim about drafting help. It does not test his separate argument that this will end with AI deciding rewards.
He gives no date for the document. My reading is that it was current guidance when the post went out, covering the 2024 review cycles. This is flagged as an ambiguity.
criteria.support_condition: A Microsoft document, Microsoft statement, or independent report that has seen the guidance confirms that Microsoft told managers to use Copilot to summarize direct reports' Connects/Perspectives/feedback as a basis for drafting reward or promotion justifications.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Microsoft guidance or credible reporting from the period shows managers were barred from using Copilot this way, or shows that no such instruction existed.
